class.name: HEGoAssetNode
class.brief_description: Represents an instantiated Houdini Digital Asset (HDA) node.
class.description:
Use this class to instantiate an HDA by operator name, set parameters, cook, and fetch output data.
Call [method HEGoBaseNode.instantiate] after assigning [member op_name]. Most data-access methods require a valid instantiated node; when called before instantiation they log an error and return a failed task.
All methods that interact with Houdini Engine return an [HEGoTask]. Await the task to get the result, through the node's [HEGoAssetAgent], called [code]hego[/code] in every example here: [codeblock] var task = asset_node.cook() var result = await agent.task(task) [/codeblock]
[method fetch_points] expects a resource compatible with [code]HEGoFetchPointsConfig[/code]. [method fetch_surfaces] expects a resource compatible with [code]HEGoFetchSurfacesConfig[/code].

method.name: reload_definition
method.description: Reloads the on-disk library that Houdini selected for this instance. The task returns the library path after confirming it contains the selected operator. [method HEGoAssetAgent.rebuild_asset] also replaces the instance and clears the host's input chains.

method.name: cook
method.description:
Submits a cook task for this asset node.
Returns an [HEGoTask] that completes with [code]0[/code] once the cook has finished, and that [b]fails[/b] when Houdini refuses to start the cook or the cook comes back with fatal errors. Awaiting it therefore gives [code]null[/code] on either kind of failure, which is what a script should check before reading the output.
A cook that finishes with non-fatal errors succeeds: Houdini reports those as warnings and the geometry is still usable.

method.name: fetch_curves
method.description:
Submits a task to fetch all curve parts from the cooked asset.
The task result is an [Array] of [Dictionary] entries. Each curve entry contains: [code]type[/code]: curve type, one of [code]CURVE_TYPE_BEZIER[/code], [code]CURVE_TYPE_NURBS[/code], or [code]CURVE_TYPE_LINEAR[/code]. [code]order[/code]: curve order. [code]positions[/code]: [PackedVector3Array] of control point positions for this curve. [code]knots[/code]: [PackedFloat32Array] of knot values, present only when the curve has knots. [code]prim_attribs[/code]: [Array] of {[code]name[/code], [code]value[/code]} dictionaries for each attribute listed in [code]read_prim_attribs[/code]. [code]point_attribs[/code]: [Array] of {[code]name[/code], [code]value[/code]} dictionaries for each attribute listed in [code]read_point_attribs[/code]. [code]is_closed[/code]: A boolean indicating whether the curve is closed.
The task result is an empty array when the node is not instantiated, the session is invalid, or geometry cannot be read.

method.name: fetch_heightfield_layer_image
method.description:
Submits a task to fetch one heightfield layer as an [Image] from the specified part id.
The task result is an [Image], or an invalid image reference when the node is not instantiated or the requested part cannot be read.

method.name: get_output_summary
method.description:
Submits a task returning what the last cook produced, so an output handler with nothing to do can be skipped without asking Houdini for attributes that are not there.
The result is a [Dictionary] with [code]has_mesh[/code], [code]has_points[/code], [code]has_curves[/code] and [code]has_volumes[/code] flags, plus [code]point_attributes[/code] and [code]prim_attributes[/code] listing the attribute names the geometry carries. It is empty when the output cannot be read.
Costs only the attribute name lookups, which are cached per cook like every other read.

method.name: get_point_output
fetch_points
method.deprecated: Use [method get_point_output] instead. Fetch configs are kept only so existing projects can move across.
method.description:
Submits a task to fetch point data using a point-fetch configuration resource.
[b]Deprecated.[/b] [method get_point_output] does the same thing from code, decides at runtime, and keeps the attribute names next to the code that reads them. Both share one implementation and one per-cook cache, so results are identical.
Config fields are interpreted as follows: [code]filter_attribs[/code] and [code]filter_attrib_values[/code]: paired by index; a point is kept only if all [code]point_attr == filter_value[/code] checks pass. [code]filter_attribs[/code] and [code]filter_attrib_values[/code] should have the same length. [code]read_attribs[/code]: extra point attributes to fetch at leaf level (in addition to [code]P[/code], which is always included). [code]split_attribs[/code]: point attributes used to build nested dictionary groups.
The method reads from the display mesh part of the cooked node.
The task result is a [Dictionary] with the following structure: If [code]split_attribs[/code] is empty, the result is a flat dictionary with leaf keys. If [code]split_attribs[/code] is non-empty, each split attribute adds one nesting level keyed by that attribute's value. Leaf dictionaries contain: [code]ids[/code]: filtered point indices in the source point array. [code]P[/code]: [Array] of [Vector3] positions. Additional keys from [code]read_attribs[/code], each mapped to an [Array] aligned with [code]ids[/code].
Returns an empty dictionary when no points pass filters, when no mesh part exists, or when geometry query fails.

method.name: get_surface_output
fetch_surfaces
method.deprecated: Use [method get_surface_output] instead. Fetch configs are kept only so existing projects can move across.
method.description:
Submits a task to fetch surface data using a surface-fetch configuration resource.
[b]Deprecated.[/b] [method get_surface_output] does the same thing from code. Both share one implementation and one per-cook cache, so results are identical.
Config fields are interpreted as follows: [code]normal[/code], [code]color[/code], [code]uv[/code], [code]uv2[/code], [code]tangents[/code]: toggles for point-derived channels included in generated Godot surface arrays. [code]custom_attribs[/code]: up to four point attributes exported as [code]ARRAY_CUSTOM0..3[/code] (RGBA float), as in [method get_surface_output]. [code]read_attribs[/code], [code]filter_attribs[/code], [code]filter_attrib_values[/code], [code]split_attribs[/code]: primitive-attribute lists used for metadata readback, filtering, and grouping. [code]filter_attribs[/code] and [code]filter_attrib_values[/code] are paired by index. [code]filter_attribs[/code] and [code]filter_attrib_values[/code] should have the same length.
The method reads the display mesh part.
The task result is a [Dictionary] with the following structure: If [code]split_attribs[/code] is empty, the root is a single leaf dictionary. If [code]split_attribs[/code] is non-empty, result is nested by split attribute values. Each leaf contains: [code]surface_array[/code]: a Godot [code]Mesh.ARRAY_MAX[/code]-sized array usable with [code]ArrayMesh.add_surface_from_arrays()[/code], including at minimum vertices and indices; optional channels are present depending on config and source attributes. [code]ids[/code]: filtered primitive ids local to the current filtered set. Any primitive attributes requested through [code]read_attribs[/code], each as an [Array] aligned with [code]ids[/code].
Returns an empty dictionary when no mesh part exists, no faces are available, no elements pass filters, or when geometry query fails.

method.name: get_heightfield_layers
method.description:
Submits a task to return available heightfield layers from the cooked asset.
Use [code]read_prim_attribs[/code] to request primitive attributes that should be included in each returned layer entry.
The task result is an [Array] where each entry is a [Dictionary] containing layer metadata such as part id, layer name, voxel dimensions, scale, and transform information.

method.name: get_help_page
method.description: Reads the live Houdini operator's help. The result is a [Dictionary] with [code]text[/code] (the complete authored help markup), [code]url[/code] (the operator's help URL) and [code]op_name[/code] (the full operator name including category). Each missing text or URL is an empty [String]. The task fails if the live operator or its help metadata cannot be read.

method.name: get_input_names
method.description:
Submits a task to return the input names defined on this HDA node.
The task result is a [PackedStringArray] of input names. This is useful for mapping script-side inputs to operator input slots.

method.name: get_node_parm_candidates
method.description: Checks the supplied live [HEGoBaseNode] sources against the Houdini node type and flags accepted by [param parm_name]. The result is an [Array] containing one [bool] per candidate in the original order. Empty, reset, incompatible and self references yield [code]false[/code]. The task fails if the owner or its single-node parameter is unavailable.

method.name: get_parms_dict
method.description:
Reads the live Houdini interface. The task returns a [Dictionary] keyed by visible top-level parameter name. Folder contents are under [code]children[/code]. Each [code]instances[/code] entry holds the child descriptors of one multiparm or ramp key.
Each descriptor includes [code]type[/code], [code]script_type[/code], [code]size[/code], [code]visible[/code], [code]disabled[/code], UI and hard range flags and bounds. [code]values[/code] holds evaluated components. String and path controls also expose authored [code]raw_values[/code]. Menus supply [code]choice_list_type[/code], [code]use_menu_item_token_as_value[/code] and, when populated, [code]choices[/code] with each option's label and token.
The [code]help[/code] string contains the first paragraph of the matching entry in the asset's embedded parameter documentation. Houdini wiki entries match by [code]#id[/code], including multiparm template names. An entry without an ID can match a unique parameter label. If no entry matches, the string contains the parameter template's explicit help, which can be empty. See [method get_help_page] for the complete document.
A folder list identifies its consecutive sibling folders with [code]folder_ids[/code]. Radio selection is the single integer in [code]values[/code]. Ordinary multiparms expose [code]multiparm_style[/code], ramps expose [code]ramp_type[/code], and instance children expose [code]template_name[/code]. For node parameters [code]node_id[/code] is the current session's resolved target or [code]-1[/code]. Read the descriptors again after a structural edit, parameter callback, cook or asset rebuild. A HAPI read error fails the task.

method.name: get_preset
method.description:
Submits a task to serialize current parameter state as a Houdini preset blob.
The task result is a [PackedByteArray]. Use together with [method set_preset] to save and restore HDA parameter setups.

method.name: insert_multiparm_instance
method.description: Inserts an instance before [param index] in the multiparm with [param parm_id]. The first position is [code]instance_start_offset[/code]. To append, use that offset plus [code]instance_count[/code]. Await completion and read [method get_parms_dict] again before editing the new instance. A stale owner, invalid position or HAPI error fails the task.

method.name: instantiate
method.description:
Submits a task to instantiate the HDA node from [member op_name].
If [member op_name] is empty, the task fails with an error.
On success, the created node id is stored and this wrapper is registered in the session manager.

method.name: remove_multiparm_instance
method.description: Removes the instance at [param index] in the multiparm with [param parm_id]. Valid positions begin at [code]instance_start_offset[/code]. Refresh [method get_parms_dict] after completion to obtain the updated instance identities and indices. A stale owner, invalid position or HAPI error fails the task.

method.name: set_node_parm
method.description: Binds a compatible, instantiated [param source] to a single Houdini node-reference parameter. Pass [code]null[/code] to clear the reference. A successful task returns [code]0[/code]. Setting the current binding again skips the write. An incompatible source, stale session or rejected operation fails the task. Reapply a durable source reference after an asset or session rebuild. Operator-path lists use the text form of [method set_parm].

method.name: set_parm
method.description:
Sets a parameter by its Houdini name. Use a number for a scalar, a matching Godot vector for numeric tuples of two to four components, or a typed packed numeric array for any numeric tuple. The element count must match the declared tuple. Floats must be finite, integers must fit int32, and integer inputs to float storage must be exactly representable. Houdini's hard limits apply.
Toggles also accept a [bool]. RGB and RGBA controls accept [Color] or a matching vector. RGB uses the first three channels. Use a [String] for a scalar string, authored file path or literal Houdini node path, and a [PackedStringArray] for a string tuple. To select a radio folder, pass its zero-based tab index. Integer writes to a button invoke its callback.
[codeblock] await agent.task(asset.set_parm("rgb", Color(2.0, 0.5, 0.1))) await agent.task(asset.set_parm("words", PackedStringArray(["east", "west"]))) [/codeblock] A successful task returns [code]0[/code]. Await the task before cooking or saving the result.

method.name: set_parms_batch
method.description: Submits one scheduled task for the parameter names and values in [param parms]. Keys may be [String] or [StringName]. Value rules match [method set_parm]. The task captures the input, validates the whole batch, then resolves each live parameter again before writing it. Invalid input fails before the first write. If Houdini rejects a later write or a callback changes the layout, earlier writes may have taken effect. Read [method get_parms_dict] before retrying.

method.name: set_preset
method.description:
Submits a task to apply a serialized Houdini parameter preset to this asset.
The preset payload should come from [method get_preset] or a compatible Houdini preset source.

members.member: Houdini operator name used by [method HEGoBaseNode.instantiate] to create the asset node.
